overview: Two records: a 1935 Dairen despatch on 775 imported American Merino sheep for a Manchurian wool-boosting crossbreeding program, and a 1934 memo on whether to forward an American firm's crude-oil sale proposal to the Manchuria Oil Company.

subfiles.title: Despatch on importing American sheep to increase Manchurian wool production
subfiles.from: Stuart E. Grummon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Reports the arrival at Dairen of American Merino sheep intended for crossbreeding and improvement of Manchuria’s wool yield.
subfiles.summary: Grummon reports 775 Merino sheep from Utah/Wyoming/Nevada landed at Dairen for Manchukuo crossbreeding, mostly to the Industry Department; native sheep yield 2.5 pounds of wool versus 7-10 for crossbreds, aiming to raise output from 9 million to 28-40 million pounds.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on proposed crude-oil sale to the Manchuria Oil Company
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Tokyo Embassy despatch concerning whether an American crude-oil sales letter should be delivered to the Manchuria Oil Company through the consular service.
subfiles.summary: Memo on Export Petroleum Company's crude-oil sale proposal to Manchuria Oil Company: Dairen's consul withheld it given unusual oil-trade conditions, Grew agreed, and lacking Department guidance, officials favored returning it to the sender.

interest: Shows a Manchukuo sheep-crossbreeding program boosting wool output, plus a separate unrelated oil-sale memo.
